strings.d1.s0.name: Stanley Park Seawall Bike Ride
strings.d1.s0.tips: Rent a bike from Denny's or Spokes (15 CAD for 2 hours). The seawall is 9 km long and passes under Lions Gate Bridge and by Third Beach.
strings.d1.s1.name: Stanley Park Totem Poles
strings.d1.s1.tips: The totem poles at Brockton Point, a First Nations site.
strings.d1.s2.name: Vancouver Aquarium
strings.d1.s2.tips: Inside the park; sea otters and the Amazon gallery.
strings.d1.s3.name: Prospect Point Cafe
strings.d1.s3.tips: A park cafe with views of the bridge.
strings.d1.s4.name: Coal Harbour Seawall & Canada Place
strings.d1.s4.tips: The terminal with its sail-shaped roof. Try FlyOver Canada (35 CAD) and watch seaplanes take off and land.
strings.d1.b0.name: Cardero's Coal Harbour
strings.d1.b0.tips: A marina restaurant; order the salmon.
strings.d1.b1.name: Vancouver Lookout Harbour Centre
strings.d1.b1.tips: An observation tower; a swap for the aquarium.
strings.d2.s0.name: Granville Island Public Market
strings.d2.s0.tips: An artists' island under the bridge. Try Lee's Donuts and the salmon, and take the Aquabus ferry (5 CAD) to get there.
strings.d2.s1.name: Granville Island Artist Studios
strings.d2.s1.tips: Glass and ceramics, the Net Loft and the Kids Market.
strings.d2.s2.name: Kitsilano Beach
strings.d2.s2.tips: A winter beach walk with snowy mountain views.
strings.d2.s3.name: Sophie's Cosmic Cafe Kitsilano
strings.d2.s4.name: Museum of Anthropology UBC
strings.d2.s4.tips: Bill Reid's Raven sculpture and totem poles, in a glass building on the UBC campus.
strings.d2.b0.name: Vanier Park & Museum of Vancouver
strings.d2.b0.tips: A space centre and the city museum; a closer alternative to the MOA.
strings.d2.b1.name: Go Fish Granville
strings.d2.b1.tips: A fish taco shack on the dock.
strings.d3.s0.name: Capilano Suspension Bridge Park
strings.d3.s0.tips: A 137 m suspension bridge, plus Treetops and Cliffwalk. A free shuttle runs from Canada Place and is quiet at 09:00. In winter, see the Canyon Lights.
strings.d3.s1.name: Grouse Mountain Skyride
strings.d3.s1.tips: Skiing and snowshoeing in winter, plus sleigh rides. The bears are hibernating.
strings.d3.s2.name: Grouse Mountain Altitudes Bistro
strings.d3.s2.tips: Lunch at the summit with views over the city.
strings.d3.s3.name: Lynn Canyon Park
strings.d3.s3.tips: A free suspension bridge and the 30 Foot Pool; Capilano's free cousin.
strings.d3.b0.name: Lonsdale Quay Market
strings.d3.b0.tips: The market by the SeaBus terminal in North Vancouver.
strings.d3.b1.name: Deep Cove
strings.d3.b1.tips: Rent a canoe or hike to Quarry Rock, and try the Honey Doughnuts. A swap for Lynn.
strings.d4.s0.name: Sea to Sky Highway Shannon Falls
strings.d4.s0.tips: Take the bus (Skylynx or YVR) for 2 hours. On the way, stop at the 335 m waterfall and see the Stawamus Chief.
strings.d4.s1.name: Sea to Sky Gondola Squamish
strings.d4.s1.tips: A gondola up to 885 m, with a suspension bridge and fjord views.
strings.d4.s2.name: Whistler Village
strings.d4.s2.tips: The Olympic village pedestrian zone, with the rings and shops.
strings.d4.s3.name: Peak 2 Peak Gondola
strings.d4.s3.tips: A record-breaking gondola (3 km) between Whistler and Blackcomb. Summit hikes and glacier views in summer, skiing in winter.
strings.d4.s4.name: Purebread Whistler
strings.d4.s4.tips: A legendary bakery for scones and cakes. Then catch the bus back.
strings.d4.b0.name: Brandywine Falls
strings.d4.b0.tips: A 70 m waterfall; a free alternative to the gondola.
strings.d4.b1.name: Araxi Whistler
strings.d5.s0.name: Gastown Steam Clock
strings.d5.s0.tips: The steam clock whistles every 15 minutes. Look around Gassy Jack Square and its cobblestones.
strings.d5.s1.name: Dr. Sun Yat-Sen Classical Chinese Garden
strings.d5.s1.tips: The first Ming-style garden outside China. The neighbouring park is free.
strings.d5.s2.name: Phnom Penh
strings.d5.s2.tips: Cambodian-Vietnamese food. Order the chicken wings and beef luc lac, and expect a queue.
strings.d5.s3.name: Yaletown
strings.d5.s3.tips: A former warehouse district. See the Roundhouse locomotive, David Lam Park and the False Creek seawall.
strings.d5.s4.name: Japadog Robson
strings.d5.s4.tips: Japanese-style hot dogs (try the terimayo) on Robson Street.
strings.d5.b0.name: Meat & Bread Gastown
strings.d5.b1.name: Vancouver Art Gallery
strings.d5.b1.tips: The Emily Carr collection; a swap for the police museum.
strings.d6.theme: Queen Elizabeth Park and Commercial Drive
strings.d6.s0.name: Queen Elizabeth Park
strings.d6.s0.tips: The city's highest point, with quarry gardens and the skyline. The Bloedel Conservatory costs 8 CAD.
strings.d6.s1.name: VanDusen Botanical Garden
strings.d6.s1.tips: A 22-hectare garden with a maze; the Festival of Lights runs in winter.
strings.d6.s2.name: Main Street Vintage
strings.d6.s2.tips: Vintage and design shops in Mount Pleasant, plus murals (August festival).
strings.d6.s3.name: Commercial Drive
strings.d6.s3.tips: Little Italy. Try the coffee at Cafe Calabria, Havana, and the sandwiches at La Grotta del Formaggio.
strings.d6.s4.name: Trout Lake Park
strings.d6.s4.tips: A neighbourhood lake with a farmers' market on Saturdays.
strings.d6.b0.name: Vij's Restaurant
strings.d6.b0.tips: Canada's famous Indian restaurant on Cambie. No reservations, so expect a queue.
strings.d6.b1.name: Science World
strings.d6.b1.tips: A science museum in a spherical building on False Creek; a swap for the garden (with kids).
strings.d7.s0.name: English Bay Beach
strings.d7.s0.tips: See the A-maze-ing Laughter sculptures and the Inukshuk on a morning walk.
strings.d7.s1.name: Davie Village
strings.d7.s1.tips: Rainbow crosswalks and cafes in the West End.
strings.d7.s2.name: Medina Cafe
strings.d7.s2.tips: The city's most famous brunch spot. Try the waffles and tagine, and expect a queue.
strings.d7.s3.name: Waterfront Canada Line YVR
strings.d7.s3.tips: The Canada Line reaches the airport in 25 minutes. Time to say goodbye.
strings.d7.b0.name: Breka Bakery Davie
strings.d7.b1.name: Roedde House Museum
strings.d7.b1.tips: A Victorian house in the West End; a swap for Davie.
strings.note0: Use the Compass card for SkyTrain, buses and SeaBus (to North Vancouver). The Canada Line to YVR takes 25 minutes (5 CAD extra). Free shuttles to Capilano and Grouse leave from Canada Place.
strings.note1: Winter is 3-8°C and rainy (Raincouver). Ski at Whistler and Grouse; the Capilano and VanDusen lights run in December; the cherry blossom festival is in April.
strings.note2: The 12% tax is not included in prices, and tips run to 18%. Capilano is pricey at 75 CAD (Lynn is free), Grouse is 80 CAD and the Whistler bus is 50-70 CAD.
strings.note3: Try salmon, sushi (Miku aburi), Japadog and spot prawns (May). Have breakfast at Granville Market.
strings.note4: Book the Whistler bus (Skylynx) days ahead. Peak 2 Peak is cheaper on summer weekdays; combine it with the Sea to Sky Gondola.
strings.note5: Apply for the Canada eTA online. Vancouver is safe; just pass through the Downtown Eastside (Hastings) without stopping.
